negative_findings.description: No EBRD project or technical-assistance operation dedicated specifically to Montenegro payment-systems modernisation was found. EBRD's Montenegro financial-sector activity surfaced as SME credit lines, guarantees, 'Go Digital in the Western Balkans' and financial-stability advisory rather than a payments-infrastructure project.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned SME/green/digital finance operations only; the payments-infrastructure role in Montenegro is carried by Banca d'Italia/ECB (TIPS clone) and EPC (SEPA), not EBRD.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids over-weighting EBRD as a payments-data source for ME; collection effort should be redirected to EPC, ECB/Banca d'Italia, WBIF and the EC Reform Agenda.

negative_findings.description: The only located World Bank/IMF FSAP payment-and-settlement-system technical note for Montenegro dates from the 2015 FSAP update (published Jan 2016). No newer FSAP financial-infrastructure note for Montenegro was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: FSAP payments assessment is ~10 years old and predates PSD2 transposition, SEPA accession and TIPS clone.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The richest independent payments-infrastructure diagnostic is stale; current benchmarking must lean on EC reports, EPC and ECB/Banca d'Italia material instead.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin/Serbian-language EBRD, World Bank or IMF diagnostic on Montenegro's payments market was located; IFI assessment material for this cell exists in English only, while local-language coverage of the same events comes from CBCG, gov.me and media rather than the assessing institutions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language searches surfaced government and media coverage (bankar.me, slobodnaevropa.org, eu.me, cbcg.me) but no IFI assessment translations.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language collection for this cell should target CBCG/gov.me/Skupstina primary documents, not translated IFI reports which do not appear to exist.

negative_findings.description: No EU/donor source was found that publishes Montenegro-specific card, ATM/POS or cash-usage statistics as a structured dataset. ECB payments statistics (SDW/Data Portal) cover EU/EEA reporting agents; Montenegro is not an ECB reporting country despite euroisation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Cell yields narrative and milestone data, plus institution-level SEPA adherence counts, but not time-series card/ATM/POS statistics.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card/ATM/POS series for ME must be sourced from CBCG's own payment statistics (a different cell), not from EU/IFI publishers.

negative_findings.description: Montenegrin government documents are served from wapi.gov.me under opaque UUID download URLs with no discoverable index, so systematic enumeration of Chapter 4 working-group reports and negotiating positions is not possible by crawling alone.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only individually search-surfaced PDFs were reachable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must use search-engine harvesting or the eu.me portal as the entry point rather than a site crawl.

brief: For Montenegro's payments market, the EU/IFI layer is unusually rich because the country is a first-mover: it entered SEPA geographical scope in November 2024, reached operational SEPA use in October 2025, and hosts the first live Banca d'Italia TIPS-clone instant-payment deployment. The authoritative assessors are therefore the European Commission (annual enlargement report, Chapter 4 closed provisionally in December 2025; plus the Growth Plan Reform Agenda with conditioned, monitored milestones), the European Payments Council (SEPA scheme-country list and the institution-level Register of Participants), and the ECB/Banca d'Italia pair for instant-payments infrastructure. Domestic-language counterparts — eu.me, gov.me/wapi document repository, CBCG press releases and the Parliament's payment-law record — supply the dated legislative and commitment detail that the EU-side documents summarise. The clear weaknesses of this cell are that no EU or IFI publisher issues Montenegro-specific card/ATM/POS or cash-usage series, and the only deep independent payments-infrastructure diagnostic (the World Bank/IMF FSAP financial-infrastructure technical note) dates from the 2015 FSAP update.
